posthog.privacyDescription: Allowed: event names, runtime/version, model/provider, usage, latency, cost, tool names, status, and trace/session identifiers. Prompts, responses, tool arguments/results, files, URLs, and exception text are never sent. Product events and AI traces use the same stable, pseudonymous per-install ID; product events disable person profiles and GeoIP enrichment, while AI uses it to correlate renderer and sidecar spans. Source-IP discard is controlled by each PostHog project's privacy setting, which BYO operators own. Autocapture, replay, surveys, feature flags, and automatic exceptions stay disabled.

aliou-pi-guardrails.removeWhen: Remove when you switch to Permission Modes or the Gotgenes policy stack — never run two policy layers at once.
aliou-pi-guardrails.risk: A full-authority extension: prompts are advice, not containment. There is no OS sandbox behind them.
aliou-pi-guardrails.summary: Deterministic prompts for protected files, out-of-workspace access and dangerous commands. Four extension entry points, no model tool, no prompt injection.

gotgenes-pi-permission-system.removeWhen: Remove if you go back to Guardrails or Permission Modes — these three are mutually exclusive.
gotgenes-pi-permission-system.risk: Still not an OS sandbox. Forwarding approvals from native subagents requires the matching @gotgenes/pi-subagents, not an unrelated subprocess package.
gotgenes-pi-permission-system.summary: Fail-closed allow / ask / deny policy across tools, Bash, paths, MCP, skills, external directories and per-agent overrides. The precise option when policy detail matters more than easy onboarding.

gotgenes-pi-subagents.removeWhen: Remove unless you are running the matching Gotgenes permission system.
gotgenes-pi-subagents.risk: Only coherent as part of the Gotgenes policy stack; on its own it is a subagent package with a narrower feature set than the alternatives.
gotgenes-pi-subagents.summary: In-process subagents with native registration and ask-state forwarding into @gotgenes/pi-permission-system.

juicesharp-rpiv-ask-user-question.removeWhen: Remove if Plan Mode's own plan-only question tool is enough for how you work.
juicesharp-rpiv-ask-user-question.risk: Adds one schema and can interrupt too eagerly. Tune its guidance rather than installing a second question UI.
juicesharp-rpiv-ask-user-question.summary: One structured clarification tool with 2–4 options, previews, notes and free-form answers. No extra model call and no native dependency.

juicesharp-rpiv-todo.removeWhen: Remove only when replacing it — do not run a second todo or task-state extension beside it.
juicesharp-rpiv-todo.risk: Low. It tracks implementation progress, not conversational planning, and confusing the two leads to duplicated state.
juicesharp-rpiv-todo.summary: A visible task overlay whose state survives reload and compaction by replaying session tool calls. No disk state and no API key.

narumitw-pi-chrome-devtools.removeWhen: Cognia already ships agent-browser — remove this unless you specifically need CDP inside Pi.
narumitw-pi-chrome-devtools.risk: Attaching to a personal Chrome profile exposes logged-in pages and cookies. Prefer its isolated temporary profile.
narumitw-pi-chrome-devtools.summary: Lazily exposes native CDP capabilities for navigation, evaluation, screenshots and target selection. Five capability tools once loaded.

narumitw-pi-github-pr.removeWhen: Remove if you read PR state through explicit gh commands instead.
narumitw-pi-github-pr.risk: Repeated process and network calls; account visibility follows your gh auth. It is status only, not a review workflow.
narumitw-pi-github-pr.summary: Passive current-branch PR status through authenticated gh, refreshed periodically and after each turn. No model tool and no comment-body injection.

narumitw-pi-goal.removeWhen: Remove if you also install Workflow — the two duplicate the same lifecycle.
narumitw-pi-goal.risk: Autonomous continuation can compound cost or repeat a bad action, and runtime cost can be very high because it keeps taking turns. Use explicit token budgets and low continuation limits.
narumitw-pi-goal.summary: Session-scoped goals with guarded automatic continuation. Its after-first-goal setting delays the tool surface until a goal exists.

narumitw-pi-lsp.removeWhen: Remove if your gates already give you the same diagnostics faster.
narumitw-pi-lsp.risk: Narrower than a real IDE LSP — no general references or rename workflow. Typecheck, Rust checks and project tests stay authoritative.
narumitw-pi-lsp.summary: Targeted diagnostics and source-fix tools backed by short-lived language servers. Two additional schemas.

narumitw-pi-plan-mode.removeWhen: Remove if you let Permission Modes own planning via its own Plan mode, or if you adopt Workflow.
narumitw-pi-plan-mode.risk: Pi cannot enforce read-only at the sandbox level, so the mode is a convention the model follows rather than a boundary.
narumitw-pi-plan-mode.summary: Conversational read-only planning with an explicit completion handoff and narrow validated Git / gh inspection. Tools and plan text are present only during the workflow.

narumitw-pi-statusline.removeWhen: Remove if you adopt Atelier, which replaces the footer and the completion notification together.
narumitw-pi-statusline.risk: None to the model context. The only hazard is installing a second footer.
narumitw-pi-statusline.summary: Model, thinking level, Git, tools, context, cache, time and cost in the footer. No LLM tool and no injected text, so the model-context cost is negligible.

narumitw-pi-subagents.removeWhen: Remove if you move to pi-subagents or the Gotgenes fork — one delegation implementation only.
narumitw-pi-subagents.risk: Every task starts another paid model context, so token and latency cost can dominate everything else. Working-directory trust is not sandboxing, and the default concurrency and depth are too broad.
narumitw-pi-subagents.summary: Isolated subprocess agents with consultation and auto-routing. Blocking-only exposes four tools; All mode exposes eight.

narumitw-pi-workflow.removeWhen: Defer entirely for now — prefer plan-mode plus goal, which are separately maintained and far more used.
narumitw-pi-workflow.risk: At a much earlier version than the packages it overlaps, and installing it beside plan-mode or goal duplicates state machines.
narumitw-pi-workflow.summary: Combines plan and goal lifecycle in one package. Its own source labels it experimental.

narumitw-pi-worktree.removeWhen: Remove if you never branch through worktrees.
narumitw-pi-worktree.risk: User-driven Git mutation. Note that a worktree is exactly where the Permission Modes sandbox stops containing.
narumitw-pi-worktree.summary: Interactive /worktree session switching. No model tool and no background work, so effectively zero prompt cost.

pi-atelier.removeWhen: Use it instead of statusline plus a notification package, never alongside them.
pi-atelier.risk: Young and broad: it replaces several separate UI packages at once, so a regression affects all of them together.
pi-atelier.summary: A responsive footer and sidebar with context thresholds, session and compaction controls, and completion notification in one package. No model tools.

pi-finish-notification.removeWhen: Remove if you install Atelier, which already supplies notifications. Otherwise review the source first.
pi-finish-notification.risk: Only 102 monthly and 22 weekly downloads, with limited source and maintenance evidence on its package metadata.
pi-finish-notification.summary: A completion notification and nothing else. Tiny footprint and no model context.

pi-mcp-adapter.removeWhen: Keep exactly one adapter. Remove this only if you replace it — never run it alongside pi-codemcp or pi-mcp-tools.
pi-mcp-adapter.risk: MCP servers execute local or remote tools and can receive repository data. Promoted tools cost roughly 150–300 tokens each; the adapter itself warns past 75.
pi-mcp-adapter.summary: Pi's only route to MCP: one lazy proxy tool, a disk metadata cache, reconnect and keepalive, and optional promotion of selected tools to direct schemas.

pi-memory.removeWhen: Remove if Cognia's own long-term memory already covers this; running both means two competing recall paths.
pi-memory.risk: Seven schemas plus recalled content are a meaningful per-turn tax, deep search can take around ten seconds, and stale private facts persist. Project ADRs and AGENTS.md must stay the source of truth.
pi-memory.summary: Seven memory tools over Markdown storage, with stable snapshots and optional qmd semantic indexing.

pi-permission-modes.removeWhen: Remove in a worktree, where its sandbox is no longer containment — keep Guardrails or use whole-process isolation instead.
pi-permission-modes.risk: Only model Bash is OS-sandboxed; file tools are policy-gated and approved escapes run unsandboxed. Worktrees degrade to prompts because the sandbox cannot handle a .git file. Never cycle to YOLO.
pi-permission-modes.summary: Allow / ask / deny with Bash AST gating, macOS sandbox-exec, a network allowlist and tool / skill gating. Injects one sandbox section every turn.

pi-permission-system-legacy.removeWhen: Avoid on Pi 0.84.1. Use @gotgenes/pi-permission-system, and reconsider after a compatible release.
pi-permission-system-legacy.risk: Its npm peer range enumerates Pi versions only through 0.80, not 0.84.1, so it is not declared compatible with the Pi that Cognia verifies against.

pi-rtk-optimizer.removeWhen: Turn compaction off — or remove it — for audits and hard debugging, where the full output is the point.
pi-rtk-optimizer.risk: Compaction can hide evidence and invalidate exact edit anchors. Start in suggestion mode with lossy source filtering off.
pi-rtk-optimizer.summary: Rewrites supported shell commands through the installed rtk binary and compacts noisy Bash, read and grep output.

pi-subagents.removeWhen: Remove if a bounded blocking-only delegation package covers your workload.
pi-subagents.risk: Much broader than the Narumitw package and much easier to over-configure. Its child processes do not natively forward Gotgenes ask prompts, so keep children read-only or give them explicit non-interactive deny policies.
pi-subagents.summary: Rich subprocess delegation with workflows, a fleet UI, MCP selection, schedules and background runs.

pi-web-access.removeWhen: Remove if Cognia's own web tools already cover your retrieval needs.
pi-web-access.risk: Broad outbound network and a wide provider / credential surface. Fetched content, not the schemas, is the real context cost. Keep remote hosted fetchers disabled and never paste keys into JSON.
pi-web-access.summary: Four tools: search, fetch, bounded cached retrieval and claim checking, with GitHub, PDF and video support.

vtstech-pi-long-term-memory.removeWhen: Not recommended at all: prefer pi-memory's explicit retrieval.
vtstech-pi-long-term-memory.risk: Its own package page documents roughly 4K tokens injected on every turn — by far the largest fixed cost in this catalog — against only 191 monthly downloads in the observed snapshot.
vtstech-pi-long-term-memory.summary: Automatic long-term memory injection with three tools.

Follow the provider's current official desktop-sync documentation at {docsUrl}; use browser automation or a relevant skill if available. webdav.aiPrompt: Help me configure encrypted WebDAV backup in Cognia for {provider}. Use the provider's current official documentation at {docsUrl}; if browser automation or a relevant skill is available, use it to inspect the settings screen and guide the configuration. Never ask me to paste a password, app password, encryption passphrase, private server URL, or other secret into chat. Explain where I should enter secrets locally, verify the correct endpoint and authentication method, have me use Test connection, save the settings, explain the separate zero-knowledge sync passphrase and its remember-on-device trade-off, then run Sync now and verify the result. If a required value is unknown, ask only for non-secret context and give precise provider-specific instructions.

descriptions.a2ui: Agent-to-UI mini-apps, runtime defaults, MCP bridge, and debugger.
descriptions.about: Version, build, diagnostics, updates and credits.
descriptions.account: Your identity, plan usage, profile, subscription and paired devices in one place.
descriptions.agentModes: Built-in and custom agent modes — system prompt, tool list, output format and live preview presets.
descriptions.agentRuntime: Built-in Anthropic SDK sidecar — defaults, permission mode, always-allow tools, built-in tool categories, sidecar diagnostics, and the A2UI bridge.
descriptions.agents: External agents — Claude Code CLI, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and any custom command speaking ACP / OpenCode / HTTP.
descriptions.aiConnections: Configure AI accounts, endpoints, credentials, deployments, verification, health, and import or export.
descriptions.apiKey: Anthropic API key (used by the local sidecar).
descriptions.appearance: Theme, font scale, language and motion.
descriptions.artifacts: Auto-detect code, HTML, React, SVG, Mermaid, charts, math and Jupyter notebooks into a side-panel workspace.
descriptions.automation: Desktop UI automation — screenshot, find element, click, type, send keys. Disabled by default; gated by a three-tier permission policy with a global kill switch.
descriptions.canvas: Monaco-based code/document editor with AI actions, version history, inline suggestions, sandboxed execution and collaboration.
descriptions.ccswitch: Reuse providers, MCP servers, prompts and skills from CCSwitch — switch the active subscription with one click.
descriptions.characters: Reusable personas with their own model and skills.
descriptions.chatTemplates: Saved messages with parameters — insert them from the / menu and fill in the blanks.
descriptions.companion: Mobile companion server — bind mode (loopback / LAN), QR pairing, paired devices, and revocation.
descriptions.connections: Configure messaging platform adapters (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ...) and manage the outbound delivery queue.
descriptions.conversation: Auto titles and the conversation timeline minimap
descriptions.data: Export, import or wipe local IndexedDB data.
descriptions.desktop: Tauri-only window, autostart and tray behavior.
descriptions.diagnostics: Crash logs, recent errors, and native logging diagnostics with export bundles.
descriptions.discover: Pin, reorder, or hide the Discover categories.
descriptions.eval: Default judge model, scorers, quality gates, and cost guards for agent evaluations.
descriptions.externalBridge: MCP server that exposes Cognia's wiki, RAG, and runtime entities to external coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline). Opt-in per scope.
descriptions.externalServices: Connect SaaS, websites, APIs, MCP servers, and local apps through one governed service catalog.
descriptions.fleet: Monitor and control coding agents launched anywhere on this machine (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode), the Dynamic-Island overlay, and recent-session history.
descriptions.gateway: Local OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoint that lets external tools (Claude Code, any OpenAI client) borrow your providers, routing, and credentials.
descriptions.general: Default model, working directory, system prompt, permission mode and always-allowed tools.
descriptions.goals: Persistent chat goals (ADR-0019). Set an objective with /goal and the agent auto-continues until a judge confirms it's done, or budgets / timeouts kick in.
descriptions.hooks: Lifecycle hooks for ~/.claude/settings.json (User / Project / Local). 21 events × matcher × command-or-webhook handlers.
descriptions.logs: Log levels, transports (console / IndexedDB / native / remote / Langfuse / OpenTelemetry), retention, redaction and per-module sampling.
descriptions.lsp: Configure LSP language servers shared by the agent runtime and editor
descriptions.mcp: Model Context Protocol servers (stdio / SSE / HTTP).
descriptions.memory: Autonomous long-term memory — what the assistant remembers about you across sessions, plus extraction, recall, and privacy controls.
descriptions.modelCatalog: Search canonical models, provider offerings, aliases, capabilities, lifecycle, and routed IDs.
descriptions.network: HTTP / HTTPS / SOCKS5 proxy for all outbound network traffic. Auto-detect Clash Verge, Mihomo, V2Ray and other local proxy tools.
descriptions.notifications: Notification center channels, quiet hours, per-source mute, and retention.
descriptions.ocr: OCR providers (Mistral OCR, Google Vision, AWS Textract, Azure DI, Claude / GPT / Gemini vision, Mathpix, OCR.space, ABBYY, Nanonets, Lark) plus on-device engines (Tesseract WASM/native, Windows.Media.Ocr, Apple Vision, Android ML Kit, ocrs, PaddleOCR) and the self-hosted HTTP adapter. Includes auto-router, PDF fast-path, and result cache.
descriptions.plugins: Browse, install, configure, and govern plugins. Review permissions, scheduled jobs, devtools, and contract audits.
descriptions.presets: Reusable session configurations — system prompt plus model, tool, MCP, and skill overrides.
descriptions.proIde: Embedded VS Code install and disk usage
descriptions.profile: Your local display name, avatar and bio — synced to companion devices and included in backups.
descriptions.providers: AI provider API keys, models, and connection settings.
descriptions.remoteControl: Local HTTP listener for inbound triggers, plus webhook signing and custom headers for outbound calls.
descriptions.remoteHosts: Drive a remote Cognia host — its terminal, files, and git — from this desktop.
descriptions.sandbox: OS / microVM sandbox health and tool execution policy
descriptions.scheduledTasks: Configure cron-style automation, agent permissions, and resource limits
descriptions.search: Web search providers (Tavily, Brave, Bing, Google, Perplexity, Exa…), defaults, cache, safety and source verification.
descriptions.security: Biometric guards for sensitive actions and privacy controls
descriptions.shellLayout: Reorder or hide items in the sidebar, the top bar and the bottom bar.
descriptions.shortcuts: View and rebind every keyboard shortcut — global system hotkeys, in-app shortcuts, and editor keybindings — in one place, with conflict detection.
descriptions.skills: Reusable instruction blobs appended to system prompts.
descriptions.slashCommands: Built-in, custom, and plugin-contributed slash commands — browse, search, and copy a command into the composer.
descriptions.sourceControl: AI commit-message generation and other Git panel preferences.
descriptions.speech: Voice input (STT) language and microphone, plus read-aloud (TTS) provider, voice and auto-play.
descriptions.squads: Squads are teams of agents you can hand a conversation to. Manage the ones you have, and start new ones from a template.
descriptions.subagents: Sub-agent templates and live runtime — spawn focused workers from a parent agent for research, code review, content, or analysis sub-tasks.
descriptions.subscription: Sign in with your Claude, Codex (ChatGPT), or OpenCode subscription, monitor rate-limit windows and balances, and manage OAuth credentials in your OS keychain.
descriptions.terminal: Integrated terminal dock — default shell, font, scrollback, and per-project overrides.
descriptions.tools: Built-in shell, filesystem, git, process and environment tools — global on/off, risk levels, and always-allow management.
descriptions.usageCost: Spending limits and the local trace debug session
descriptions.workflows: Visual n8n-style orchestration over characters, teams, skills, twins, and connectors. Trigger via cron, webhook, platform message, or manual run.
descriptions.workspaceTrust: Trust folders before agents run commands in them. Untrusted workspaces run in Restricted Mode.

scopeDescriptions.agent:dispatch: ⚠ Lets external agents run your built-in/plugin subagents or characters headlessly (tool loop + model calls). Returned text is PII-redacted. Default OFF.
scopeDescriptions.agent:team: ⚠ Lets external agents start an Agent Team headlessly — a multi-agent orchestration they couldn't otherwise reach. Default OFF.
scopeDescriptions.inbound:write: ⚠ Lets external agents contribute lessons, skill drafts, and notes. Nothing is applied automatically — submissions land in a review queue as pending, untrusted drafts for you to accept or discard. Default OFF.
scopeDescriptions.inbox:connectors:read: ⚠ Read-only inbox introspection — adapters, conversations, drafts, audit. Metadata may include conversation handles and recent message snippets. Default OFF.
scopeDescriptions.inbox:connectors:send: ⚠ Lets external agents enqueue AI replies to your IM inbox. Goes through the same pipeline as in-app chat (PII gate, policy, outbound queue). Default OFF.
scopeDescriptions.mcp:computer-use: ⚠ Drives the host computer (mouse / keyboard / screenshot) from external coding agents. Honours Settings → Automation → Permissions; per-call tier surfaces the consent overlay.
scopeDescriptions.memory:read: ⚠ Lets external agents search and list what the assistant remembers about you — distilled personal facts, same sensitivity tier as twin retrieval. Default OFF.
scopeDescriptions.memory:write: ⚠ Lets external agents store, update, and forget long-term memories. Writes are PII-screened, tagged as external, and can never change the assistant's working instructions. Default OFF.
scopeDescriptions.plugin:tools: ⚠ Lets external agents invoke your plugin-registered tools. The plugin's own consent gate + ownership check still apply per call. Default OFF.
scopeDescriptions.rag:twin: ⚠ Retrieval over your digital twin's chunks (personal documents / chat / code). Default OFF.
scopeDescriptions.rag:user-repo: Retrieval over user-supplied repos. Phase 3 — disabled.
scopeDescriptions.runtime:characters: ⚠ Exposes character configs (may contain personal prompts).
scopeDescriptions.runtime:plugins: Exposes the list and metadata of installed plugins.
scopeDescriptions.runtime:twins: ⚠ Exposes Twin profiles. PII redaction has run, but review before enabling.
scopeDescriptions.wiki:cognia: Public Cognia code wiki — safe to expose.
scopeDescriptions.wiki:user-repo: Wiki for user-supplied repos. Phase 3 — disabled in Phase 1.
scopeDescriptions.workflow:run: ⚠ Lists and runs active immutable workflow deployments, reads their durable events, and can cancel runs. Default OFF.

Context that looks like a secret (API keys, tokens, credentials) is detected and skipped. Plugin-contributed providers are unaffected by this setting.

toolSettings.alwaysAllowDesc: Tools the user has approved across the board. Future calls skip the approval dialog.
toolSettings.alwaysAllowEmpty: No tools have been added to the always-allow list yet.
toolSettings.astGrepDesc: AST-aware code search and refactoring (ast_grep_search / ast_grep_replace) across 25 languages, backed by the ast-grep CLI. Matches code structure with meta-variables ($VAR, $$$), not plain text. Desktop only; the binary is probed lazily.
toolSettings.codeGraphDesc: Structural code intelligence over a tree-sitter symbol graph (codegraph_search / node / callers / callees / impact / context / explore / files). Sub-millisecond queries grep can't answer: where a symbol is defined, who calls it, and blast radius. Read-only; desktop only.
toolSettings.coreFilesDesc: Full coding-agent toolkit for non-Anthropic models: search, read, patch, shell, waitable background commands, and structured session tasks with dependencies. Read-only tools run freely; filesystem and shell mutations require per-call approval.
toolSettings.dependencyResearchDesc: Clone a dependency's source repository into an ignored .cognia/clonedeps/ workspace (clone_dep_source / list_cloned_deps) so the agent can read library internals. HTTPS only, idempotent, no build scripts run. Desktop only.
toolSettings.description: Per-category toggles for the in-process cognia-tools MCP server. Each category exposes a different set of tools to the agent.
toolSettings.desktopRequiredDesc: These tools run inside the local sidecar process. They are unavailable in the web build.
toolSettings.environmentManagementDesc: Read environment variables and system info. Secret-shaped keys (KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD) are redacted unless the agent explicitly opts in.
toolSettings.fileExtrasDesc: hash, diff, content_search, file_info and other ops not covered by the SDK's built-in Read / Write / Glob / Grep.
toolSettings.gitOperationsDesc: Structured wrappers for git status, diff, log, branch, remote, tag, and repo inspection. Read-only.
toolSettings.lspIntelligenceDesc: Language-server-backed code navigation — go-to-definition, find references, hover types, document symbols, and live diagnostics. Desktop only; language servers spawn lazily on first use.
toolSettings.permissionsDesc: Tools that require approval pop up a per-call dialog. Add a tool to the always-allow list (below) to skip the prompt. Disable a category to remove its tools from the agent entirely.
toolSettings.processManagementDesc: List, search, start and terminate local processes. Off by default — start/terminate are high-risk.
toolSettings.selfInvokeCardDesc: Let the agent call tools to drive itself — load a skill's instructions, or run a slash command. Host-routed; works in the browser and the CLI. Off by default.
toolSettings.sessionMessagingToolDesc: Let the agent discover and send untrusted plain-text requests to other live sessions in the same workspace.
toolSettings.shellExecutionDesc: Allowlist + blocklist + dangerous-pattern guard for shell commands. Off by default — overlaps SDK Bash and is high-risk.
toolSettings.skillToolDesc: Expose the Skill tool so the agent can load a skill's instructions mid-task.
toolSettings.slashToolDesc: Expose the SlashCommand tool so the agent can run a registered slash command. Built-in UI commands return guidance to run them from the composer.
toolSettings.spawnTaskToolDesc: Let the agent stage a scoped follow-up task in a named sidechat for you to review and start.
toolSettings.teamCollabToolDesc: Let teammates collaborate during a team run — message peers, share the blackboard, open or vote in a consensus, and delegate sub-tasks. Only applies to Agent Team sessions.
toolSettings.terminalReplDesc: Agent-private persistent PTY sessions backed by node-pty (lazy loaded). Use for stateful REPLs (python / sql / claude-code) where the agent needs to hold state across multiple writes. Orthogonal to the dock-relay path — REPL is invisible to the user.
toolSettings.title: Built-in tools

tools.astGrepReplace: Refactor code by AST-aware structural rewrite across 25 languages. Dry-run by default; set dry_run:false to write.
tools.astGrepSearch: Search code by AST structure (meta-variables $VAR / $$$) across 25 languages. Read-only; more precise than text grep.
tools.checkProgramAllowed: Test whether a program would be allowed to start_process.
tools.cloneDepSource: Clone a dependency's HTTPS source repo into .cognia/clonedeps/ (idempotent) so you can read its internals.
tools.codegraphCallees: What a symbol calls or references, transitively.
tools.codegraphCallers: Who calls or references a symbol, transitively.
tools.codegraphContext: Task-relevant context for a natural-language query in one call: entry-point symbols, the related subgraph, snippets, and files.
tools.codegraphExplore: Survey the neighbourhood around symbols you name explicitly. Use when you already know one or two symbol names.
tools.codegraphFiles: List indexed source files with per-file symbol counts, language, and any extraction errors.
tools.codegraphImpact: Blast radius: everything that transitively depends on a symbol. Check before changing it.
tools.codegraphNode: Fetch one symbol by id or qualified name: kind, signature, docstring, location, and verbatim source.
tools.codegraphSearch: Full-text search the graph for symbols by name or doc. Returns ranked rows whose ids feed the other codegraph tools.
tools.codegraphStatus: Report index health: file / node / edge counts, language histogram, storage backend, and files pending re-index.
tools.contentSearch: Search file contents (substring or regex) with line numbers.
tools.coreApplyPatch: Apply a unified diff across one or more files atomically (create / modify / delete).
tools.coreBash: Execute a free-form shell command (approval-gated; output keeps the tail).
tools.coreBashOutput: Read new output from a background shell started with bash(run_in_background).
tools.coreEdit: Replace an exact string in a file, with whitespace-tolerant fuzzy fallback.
tools.coreGlob: Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (newest first).
tools.coreGrep: Search file contents with a regex (ripgrep-backed; content / files / count modes).
tools.coreKillShell: Terminate a background shell started with bash(run_in_background).
tools.coreListShells: List background shells with status, working directory, timing, and exit details.
tools.coreMonitor: Wait for a background job, output pattern, shell predicate, or upstream task; long waits become durable background watches.
tools.coreMonitorCancel: Cancel a durable background watch owned by this session.
tools.coreMonitorList: List this session's active and settled background watches.
tools.coreMultiEdit: Apply multiple string replacements to one file atomically.
tools.coreNotebookEdit: Edit a Jupyter notebook cell (replace / insert / delete) by cell id or number.
tools.coreRead: Read a text file with line numbers; pages large files; lists directories.
tools.coreTaskCreate: Create a structured session task and return its stable id.
tools.coreTaskGet: Read one structured task with dependencies, owner, metadata, and timestamps.
tools.coreTaskList: List structured session tasks and their current dependency state.
tools.coreTaskUpdate: Update task state, details, ownership, metadata, dependencies, or delete it.
tools.coreTodoWrite: Update the session task list shown to the user.
tools.coreWrite: Create or overwrite a file (requires a prior read of existing files).
tools.currentTime: Get the current date and time (UTC plus a localized string for a given timezone).
tools.directoryDelete: Delete a directory. Recursive option for non-empty trees.
tools.fileAppend: Append UTF-8 text to a file. Creates the file if missing.
tools.fileBinaryWrite: Write a base64-encoded binary payload to a file.
tools.fileExists: Check if a path exists. Returns isFile / isDirectory.
tools.fileHash: Compute md5 / sha1 / sha256 / sha512 of a file. Read-only.
tools.fileMove: Move a file across or within filesystems.
tools.fileSearch: List files under a directory matching an optional glob and extension filter.
tools.getEnv: Read a single env var. Secrets are redacted unless revealed.
tools.getProcess: Get a single process by PID.
tools.getProcessManagerStatus: Sidecar process manager state and tracked PID count.
tools.getTrackedProcesses: PIDs the agent has started this session.
tools.gitCommit: Create a commit from staged changes. Requires approval.
tools.gitDiff: Diff working tree or staged area.
tools.gitHistory: Commit history for a path or set of paths.
tools.gitLog: Recent commits with hash / author / date / subject.
tools.gitRepoInspect: Top-level path, current branch, HEAD hash, upstream.
tools.gitStage: Stage files for commit (git add). Requires approval.
tools.gitTag: List tags, optionally filtered by glob.
tools.listClonedDeps: List the dependency source repos already cloned into .cognia/clonedeps/ (reads the manifest).
tools.listEnv: List process env vars. Secrets are redacted unless revealed.
tools.lspDiagnostics: Get current compiler / linter diagnostics for a file.
tools.lspDocumentSymbols: List the symbols (classes, functions, variables) defined in a file.
tools.lspFindReferences: Find all references to the symbol at a position.
tools.lspGotoDefinition: Find where the symbol at a position is defined.
tools.lspHover: Get type / signature / documentation for the symbol at a position.
tools.searchProcesses: Find processes whose name contains a substring.
tools.shellExecuteAdvanced: Run a single program with argv, gated by allowlist + blocklist + dangerous-pattern guard. Always requires approval.
tools.startProcess: Start a program from the allowlist. Requires approval.
tools.systemInfo: Platform, arch, node version, cpu, memory, uptime, hostname.
tools.terminalReplRead: Drain accumulated REPL output (default: destructive read). Returns '{data, truncated, exited, exitCode}'.
tools.terminalReplSpawn: Open a persistent interactive PTY (e.g. python / sql REPL). Returns sessionId for subsequent writes / reads.
tools.terminalReplWrite: Write bytes into a REPL session's stdin. Non-blocking — pair with terminal_repl_read.
tools.terminateProcess: Terminate a PID (default: only PIDs this session started).
tools.topMemoryProcesses: Top N processes by resident memory.
tools.webClone: Snapshot a live web page — download its HTML plus all CSS/JS/image/font assets into a self-contained single file or a directory bundle, with optional component extraction + framework codegen. Writes into the workspace.
tools.webCloneConvert: Run component extraction + framework codegen on an existing local snapshot (bundle directory or single HTML) without re-fetching. Generates Vue/React/Angular/Svelte/jQuery components.

toolSettings.vectorToolDesc: Let the agent store and recall documents in the current project's vector memory. Collections are scoped to the linked project; a session without one cannot use these tools.
toolSettings.vectorToolDesktopOnly: Requires the desktop app — vector memory runs on the local native vector store.
toolSettings.webAllowPrivateDesc: Let web_fetch reach localhost and private-network hosts (10.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x cloud metadata). Off by default to block SSRF — enable only for trusted local development.
toolSettings.webAlwaysDistillDesc: Run every fetched page through the utility model before the agent sees it, even without a question — the agent never reads raw page text, narrowing the prompt-injection surface. Needs a configured model; slightly more cost per fetch.
toolSettings.webCardDesc: Web search and fetch (web_search / web_fetch). On by default — works in the browser and the CLI. web_search needs a provider configured in Settings → Search.
toolSettings.webNativeAnthropicDesc: On the Anthropic path, use Claude's built-in WebSearch / WebFetch (server-side extraction + citations) instead of the multi-provider tools. Other providers keep the multi-provider tools.
toolSettings.webPreferCogniaDesc: Use Cognia's multi-provider search (Tavily / Brave / Exa …) even when the model's own runtime brings web search. Off means the runtime's native search is used where it exists — it needs no API key and returns citations. Needs a configured search provider.
toolSettings.webcloneDesc: Snapshot a live web page (web_clone / web_clone_convert) — download its HTML plus all CSS/JS/image/font assets into a self-contained single file or a directory bundle, with optional component extraction and Vue/React/Angular/Svelte/jQuery codegen. Private/loopback targets are blocked unless opted in. Desktop only.
